title: f17r P2: stock and donor are joined by two spring methods or a summer bud method
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. A whole 23-group paragraph is nominated as a graft-method account. Its central nine groups receive a complete speculative reading linking stock, donor shoot, two insertion methods and spring, then bark budding and summer. Method and season jointly determine whether the proposed action is licensed; surrounding preparation and outcome remain open.

design.whole_content_draft: Select the stock and donor and prepare the receiving part. For stock and donor shoot, insert either into a split or between inner bark and wood in spring; use a piece of bark for budding in summer. Judge whether the union is compatible and retain any refusal or changed-product result. Proposed whole-paragraph organization: .4 preparation/participants; .5 method-season rules; .6 acceptance/refusal and product. Only .5 currently has a complete speculative multiword gloss; .4 and .6 are explicitly not translated.
coupled_claims: Split and under-bark insertion belong to the spring branch.
Bark budding belongs to the summer branch.
Host and donor are ordered participants; compatibility or refusal governs whether a product follows.
design.joint_consequence: Changing only the season can invalidate one method while permitting another, although the same stock/donor names remain. Reversing host and donor is not guaranteed to preserve compatibility or product. A paired plant catalogue cannot infer these conditional permissions from co-occurrence alone.
concrete_rivals: A developmental leaf/flower/fruit list followed by harvesting and sowing, as in RAW368, predicts detached seeds and a planting action rather than an inserted shoot or bark union.
A free list of grafting methods without seasonal scope permits the same method-year pairing in either season.
A symmetric similarity catalogue does not require ordered host/donor or a refusal endpoint.
lexical_and_syntax_debts: All nine central meanings are guesses; this paragraph has little exact whole-form recurrence, so it cannot alone establish a reusable graft vocabulary.
No source proves that the illustrated plant is grafted; no image was inspected for this proposal.
No universal donor-trait preservation law is imposed: Palladius actually describes changed products and refusal exceptions.
The seasonal reading has no identified written disjunction/conjunction; grouping the first two methods under dair and the last under qody is a provisional constituent hypothesis.
The surrounding fourteen source groups remain UNKNOWN. No success, refusal or compatibility word is supplied merely to complete the narrative.

additional_evidence.quote: **Primary source set.** Columella, *De arboribus* 26.1.1 gives three grafting methods: a split stock receiving inserted shoots; slips inserted between inner bark and wood, with both methods assigned to spring; and budding with a piece of bark, assigned to summer. It also explicitly debates the older compatibility rule based on similarity of bark, inner bark and fruit. A readable source/translation is [ReadAncientTexts, Columella *De Arboribus*](https://readancienttexts.com/columella/de_arboribus/1); the primary-text locator is [Packard Humanities Institute 26.1.1](https://latin.packhum.org/loc/845/1/30/704-709). Palladius, *De insitione* XIV, gives directed host/donor examples in its graft poem: pear stock/donor combinations alter fruit size, taste, thorns, husk or flesh; quince refuses foreign grafting; pomegranate rejects foreign sap/foliage and exchanges its own germs. The readable Latin/French witness is [Palladius Book XIV](https://remacle.org/bloodwolf/erudits/palladius/livre14.htm).
